title: Public properties/methods, composition, slots, and lifecycle hooks
objectives: Compose a parent Lightning web component that sets public properties and calls public methods on a child.
Use unnamed and named slots so a parent can pass markup into a child template.
Place constructor work after super(), and remember public properties are not set until after construction.
Distinguish owner versus container in a parent/child containment hierarchy.
diagnostic_question: A parent template nests c-lab-child. The child reads an @api recordId as undefined in the constructor, the parent cannot call a helper that was not decorated, and markup the parent passed never appears. Which public property, method, slot, and lifecycle hook rules failed?
definition: Composition nests child Lightning web components in a parent template. The owner can set public properties, call public methods, and listen for events. Slots are placeholders for markup the parent passes in. constructor() runs parent-then-child, must call super() first, and does not yet have public properties or children. ([Compose Components](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-compose.html); [Slots](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-slots.html); [constructor hook](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-lifecycle-hooks-created.html))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for @api as the parent/child contract, slots versus properties, and the constructor trap of reading recordId too early. Treating every nested tag as a disk-nested folder (LWC-002) or shouting down with events (LWC-005) mixes later lessons into this one.
sixty_second_explanation: Picture a restaurant pass window. The parent chef writes tickets onto the child's @api properties and can call an @api method like a spoken 'fire table 4'. Slots are empty plates the parent fills with garnish markup. constructor() is unlocking the station: call super() first; tickets are not on the rail yet. connectedCallback() is when the station is on the line. Do not stuff an Aura component onto an LWC plate.
deeper_explanation: The owner is the component that owns the template. It can set public properties on composed children, call methods on them, and listen for their events. A container is weaker: it can read but not change public properties of contained components, call methods, and listen for some bubbled events. Parent/child is defined in the parent's HTML, while both folders sit as siblings under lwc. ([Compose Components](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-compose.html))

The JavaScript file documents that the public API is public properties and methods annotated with @api. Parents set those properties as HTML attributes (kebab-case). Undecorated fields stay internal. ([Component JavaScript File](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-javascript.html))

A slot is a placeholder for markup the parent passes into the child's body. Unnamed slots take default body content; named slots match slot="name". You cannot pass an Aura component into a slot. DOM passed into a slot is not in the child's shadow tree: use this.querySelector, not this.template.querySelector, to reach it. ([Slots](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-slots.html))

constructor() fires when the instance is created, parent then child. The first statement must be super() with no parameters. Do not inspect attributes, children, or public properties there—they are not ready. Properties are assigned after construction and before connectedCallback(). Add host attributes in connectedCallback(), not in the constructor. ([constructor hook](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-lifecycle-hooks-created.html))

mental_model.analogy: A restaurant pass window: @api properties are tickets the parent chef sets on the child station; @api methods are 'fire' calls; slots are empty plates the parent garnishes; constructor is unlocking the station before tickets arrive.
useful_mapping: parent template → chef side of the pass
@api method → spoken fire call the parent may invoke
constructor → unlock station; tickets not on the rail yet
connectedCallback → station is on the line
where_it_breaks: Owner versus container power is a framework rule, not kitchen rank.
Slotted markup stays in the parent's DOM identity; querySelector rules are not dinnerware.
Aura cannot go in an LWC slot even if it 'looks like garnish'.
Other lifecycle hooks (render, renderedCallback, errorCallback) are more than opening the station.

teach_back_prompt: Draw a parent/child pair: which @api properties the parent sets, which method it may call, where a named slot is filled, and why recordId is undefined in the child's constructor.

claims.claim: The owner component can set public properties on composed children, call methods on them, and listen for events. Parent/child is declared in HTML; folders remain siblings under lwc.
claims.validation: Compose Components owner/container and parent/child HTML.

claims.validation: Component JavaScript File public API bullet.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A parent composes a child in HTML, sets @api properties, may call @api methods, and fills slots with markup. constructor is too early for public properties; use connectedCallback or later.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I separate disk folders (siblings under lwc) from parent/child in the template. I decorate only the contract with @api. I use slots when the parent supplies markup, not when it supplies a record Id. I never pass Aura into an LWC slot. I call super() first and I do not read recordId in the constructor.

terminology.plain: Nesting a child Lightning web component in a parent template.
terminology.precise: Parent/child is defined in parent HTML. Folders are siblings under lwc, not nested directories.
terminology.boundary: Events up the tree are LWC-005.

terminology.plain: The component whose template contains the children.
terminology.precise: The owner can set public properties, call methods, and listen for any events fired by composed components.
terminology.non_example: A sibling on the same Lightning page that does not contain the child in its template.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: container, which cannot change public properties of contained components.
terminology.boundary: Lightning page App Builder placement is not ownership.

terminology.plain: A public field the parent may set as an attribute.
terminology.precise: Part of the component public API. Parents typically pass kebab-case attributes that map to camelCase fields.
terminology.non_example: A private field the parent tries to set without @api.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: @track, which is deep observation, not public exposure.
terminology.boundary: Do not mutate objects the parent passed; data flows down (data guidelines, LWC-006).

terminology.plain: A public function the parent may call on the child.
terminology.precise: Annotated with @api so the owner can invoke it. Undecorated methods are not the public API.
terminology.example: @api reset() { this.value = ''; } called from the parent after querySelector.
terminology.non_example: A private helper the parent calls by poking undocumented internals.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex public method, which is server visibility.
terminology.boundary: How the parent obtains the child instance (refs vs querySelector) can vary by API version—Needs verification of the preferred current pattern.

terminology.plain: A placeholder in the child template the parent fills with markup.
terminology.precise: Unnamed slot takes default body. Named slots match slot="name". Aura cannot be passed into a slot.
terminology.non_example: Passing a record Id through a slot instead of an @api property.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Visualforce facet, a different composition model.
terminology.boundary: slotchange fires only for direct children of the slot node.

terminology.plain: The hook that runs when the instance is created.
terminology.precise: Parent then child. First statement super() with no parameters. Do not inspect public properties, attributes, or children. Do not add host attributes here.
terminology.example: constructor() { super(); this.template.addEventListener is still the wrong place for host attributes. }
terminology.non_example: Reading this.recordId in constructor and treating undefined as a platform bug.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: connectedCallback, which runs after properties are assigned.

terminology.plain: The hook after the element is inserted and properties have been assigned.
terminology.precise: The constructor topic states properties are assigned after construction and before connectedCallback. Use it to add host attributes and to start work that needs public properties.
terminology.non_example: Calling super() only here and skipping constructor.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: renderedCallback, which runs after render—details Need verification on the overview page.
terminology.boundary: Unsubscribe and cleanup belong in disconnectedCallback (later lesson / overview).

terminology.plain: A middle component that wraps children but is itself inside the owner.
terminology.precise: A container can read but not change public properties of contained components, call methods, and listen for some bubbled events.
terminology.example: c-todo-wrapper between c-todo-app and c-todo-item in the Guide example.
terminology.non_example: The owner that authors the outer template.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lightning App Builder region, which is a page container, not this owner/container pair.

mechanics.failure: Nesting the child folder inside the parent folder

mechanics.trigger: Parent must pass values or call behavior
mechanics.after: @api properties and methods only for the contract
mechanics.observe: Parent attribute maps to the decorated field
mechanics.failure: Parent setting a private field by convention

mechanics.after: Slots for markup, @api for typed values

when_to_use: When a parent Lightning web component must set public properties on a child or call a public @api method.
When composition in the parent template is the right split instead of one giant component.
When the parent should pass markup into child slots rather than encoding HTML as a string property.
When lifecycle hooks matter: constructor is too early for public properties; connectedCallback runs after they are assigned.
When you must refuse Aura markup inside an LWC slot.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this composition lesson as a substitute for custom events or Lightning Message Service (LWC-005).
Do not treat @api public properties as a data-access choice versus wire or Apex (LWC-006).
Do not use slots when the parent only has a record Id—that is an @api property, not markup.
Do not invent a full lifecycle order-of-execution table beyond the constructor facts cited here.
Do not compose production customer pages from this parent/child lab.
configuration_or_code_location: constructor and connectedCallback in the child class.

worked_example.scenario: A sandbox lab needs labParent to show a LAB_ contact card. The child needs a public name, a reset method, a named footer slot, and must not read name in the constructor. No production data.
inputs: Child folder is a sibling under lwc
Footer markup supplied by the parent

decisions.decision: Decorate name and reset with @api; set name from parent attributes.
decisions.because: The public API is @api properties and methods.

decisions.decision: Put a named footer slot on the child and pass markup from the parent.
decisions.rejected: Passing HTML as an innerHTML string property

decisions.decision: Log name in connectedCallback, not constructor.
decisions.because: Public properties are assigned after construction.
decisions.rejected: Treating undefined record/name in constructor as a Salesforce bug

configuration_or_code: labChild.js: import { LightningElement, api } from 'lwc'; export default class LabChild extends LightningElement { @api name; @api reset() { this.name = ''; } constructor() { super(); } connectedCallback() { /* name is assigned */ } }
worked_example.output: Parent shows the child with name and footer markup. Constructor does not rely on name.
verification: name is undefined if read before connectedCallback in a constructor log.
Footer span appears in the named slot.
Aura component is not used inside the slot.
worked_example.self_explanation: Composition was HTML nesting plus @api plus slots plus constructor timing.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable scratch org; labParent and labChild only.
steps: Create labChild with @api label, an @api ping() method that sets a private note, and an unnamed slot plus a named slot="badge".
Create labParent that sets label on <c-lab-child>, passes inner markup into both slots, and calls ping() from a button handler using a supported child lookup.
In labChild constructor, call super() only. In connectedCallback, read this.label and confirm it is populated.

If slotted markup is missing, check slot="badge" spelling versus name="badge".

Child JS showing super() in constructor and @api members; note that label is read in connectedCallback.

decision_table.signal: Parent has a record Id or string the child must receive.
decision_table.choose: Public @api property set from the parent template attribute.
decision_table.not: A slot filled with the Id as text as the only contract.
decision_table.why: Typed values are public properties; slots are for markup.

decision_table.signal: Parent must supply heading HTML or a footer.
decision_table.choose: Child <slot> unnamed or named; parent passes markup.
decision_table.not: innerHTML assignment inside the child from a string property.
decision_table.why: Slots exist so parents pass markup into the child template.

decision_table.signal: Parent must invoke child behavior on a button.
decision_table.choose: An @api method on the child called from parent JavaScript.
decision_table.not: A private method the parent reaches by undocumented internals.
decision_table.why: The public API is @api properties and methods.

decision_table.signal: Child needs the public property during startup.
decision_table.choose: Read it in connectedCallback or later, after properties are assigned.
decision_table.not: Read it in constructor before super's world has attributes.
decision_table.why: constructor topic: properties are not passed yet; they arrive before connectedCallback.

limitations: Full hook table Needs verification from the lifecycle overview page.
Boolean @api attribute quirks Need verification on the properties page.
security_notes: Do not expose internals with @api 'just in case'.
Slotted markup still runs in the page; do not slot untrusted HTML.
recordId on a child does not bypass FLS.
common_mistakes: Passing Aura into an LWC slot.
Using this.template.querySelector to find slotted nodes.

mcqs.prompt: Where is the parent/child relationship defined?

options.A: In the parent HTML template; folders remain siblings under lwc
options.B: By nesting the child folder inside the parent folder

mcqs.rationale: Compose Components: parent-child is defined in parentComponent.html; folders sit in the same lwc directory.

distractor_explanations.C: Targets expose the parent, not the child relationship.
distractor_explanations.D: Apex does not compose LWC templates.

mcqs.prompt: What can the owner do to composed children?

options.A: Set public properties, call methods, and listen for events
options.B: Only listen for Lightning Message Service
options.C: Change child private fields by name
options.D: Nest Aura inside every slot by default

mcqs.rationale: The owner controls composed components that way.

distractor_explanations.B: LMS is cross-DOM, not the owner/child default.
distractor_explanations.C: Private fields are not the public API.
distractor_explanations.D: Aura cannot be passed into a slot.

mcqs.prompt: How do you expose a public property or method?

options.B: Name it public without a decorator

mcqs.rationale: The JS file topic: public API via @api properties and methods.

distractor_explanations.B: Undecorated fields are local to the module by default.
distractor_explanations.C: meta.xml is targets, not JS visibility.
distractor_explanations.D: Apex global is a different language.

mcqs.prompt: Can you pass an Aura component into an LWC slot?

options.A: No. You cannot pass an Aura component into a slot

mcqs.rationale: Slots topic: you can’t pass an Aura component into a slot.

distractor_explanations.D: Lifecycle does not lift the restriction.

mcqs.prompt: Why is this.recordId undefined in constructor even though the parent set record-id?

options.A: Public properties are assigned after construction and before connectedCallback

mcqs.rationale: constructor topic: properties aren’t passed yet; they are assigned before connectedCallback.

distractor_explanations.B: recordId is a common @api pattern on record pages.

mcqs.prompt: What must be the first statement in constructor()?
mcqs.rationale: Custom elements spec via the constructor topic: first statement super() with no parameters.

distractor_explanations.B: Do not inspect or assign public properties there as initialization of the contract.
distractor_explanations.D: Do not use a non-simple return.

mcqs.prompt: Slotted span is not found with this.template.querySelector('span'). What should you use?

options.A: this.querySelector('span') because slotted nodes are not in the child's shadow tree

mcqs.rationale: Slots: use this.querySelector for elements passed via slots.

distractor_explanations.B: Forbidden in constructor and not a query API.
distractor_explanations.D: template.querySelector is for the child's shadow tree.

options.A: Owner can set public properties; container can read but not change them

mcqs.rationale: Compose Components lists owner powers versus weaker container powers.

mcqs.prompt: You need to add a data attribute on the host during startup. Where?
mcqs.rationale: Do not add attributes to the host during construction; use another hook such as connectedCallback.

distractor_explanations.B: CSS is not how you set data attributes.
distractor_explanations.C: Configuration XML is not the host element.
distractor_explanations.D: super() must be first; host attributes still do not belong in constructor.

mcqs.rationale: The constructor flows from parent to child.

distractor_explanations.B: That is not the cited constructor order.

mcqs.prompt: Parent wants to pass 'Willy' into a firstName area of the child. Best tool?

options.A: A named slot firstName, or an @api firstName property if it is just a string value

mcqs.rationale: The slots example passes Willy into a named firstName slot; a string can also be an @api property. Choose slot when it is markup.

distractor_explanations.B: LMS is for cross-DOM, not parent/child defaults.
distractor_explanations.C: Aura events are the wrong model.

mcqs.prompt: slotchange did not fire when a nested footer inside slotted content toggled. Why might that be?

options.A: slotchange fires when a direct child of the slot changes, not when descendants inside that child change
options.D: You must key the slot with index

mcqs.rationale: The slots topic: changes within children of the slot do not trigger slotchange.

interview_questions.question: How do parent and child Lightning web components relate?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The parent template nests the child tag. Folders are siblings under lwc. The owner sets @api properties, may call @api methods, and can listen for events.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I distinguish owner from container. I refuse nested folders. I map kebab-case attributes to @api fields. I use slots for markup. I do not use LMS for this parent/child pair.
interview_questions.example: labParent.html nests <c-lab-child name={displayName}></c-lab-child> with labChild as a sibling bundle.
follow_ups: What can a container not do?

interview_questions.question: What is @api for on a child Lightning web component?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: It marks the public properties and methods a parent is allowed to use. Undecorated fields are not that contract.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I import api from lwc. I keep the surface small. I set properties from parent markup. I call methods from parent JS. I do not confuse @api with @track or with Apex public.

interview_questions.question: Parent needs to inject a footer into the child. Property or slot?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A slot, usually named footer, so the parent passes markup. Use @api only if it is a typed value, not HTML structure.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show unnamed versus named slots from the Guide's Willy/Wonka example. I forbid Aura in the slot. I query slotted nodes with this.querySelector. I still pass recordId as @api, not as a slot.
interview_questions.example: filled by LAB_ footer in the parent.
tradeoffs: Named slots vs a single unnamed slot
weak_answer_warnings: innerHTML as the default composition tool

interview_questions.question: recordId is undefined in the child's constructor. Is App Builder broken?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Usually no. Public properties are not assigned yet. Read recordId in connectedCallback or later after super() in constructor.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I recite parent-then-child constructor, super() first, no children, no public properties. I add host attributes in connectedCallback. If it is still undefined there, then I check the parent attribute name and the page target providing recordId.
interview_questions.example: constructor() { super(); } connectedCallback() { console.log(this.recordId); } on a record-page child.
tradeoffs: connectedCallback vs renderedCallback for DOM work
Failing fast vs waiting for the hook
follow_ups: Can you add host attributes in constructor?
What is forbidden in constructor besides properties?

interview_questions.question: Parent cannot call child.reset(). What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: reset must be @api. The parent must hold a child instance. A private method is invisible on purpose.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check the decorator import, the method spelling, and that we are not calling before the child exists. I prefer documenting the public method rather than reaching into the child's shadow. I do not turn it into an LMS message for a direct child.
interview_questions.example: Child @api reset(); parent button handler calls the child's reset after the child is rendered.
tradeoffs: Public method vs child dispatching an event
querySelector vs refs — current preferred lookup Needs verification
follow_ups: Should reset be an event instead?
When is the child instance available?

interview_questions.question: Slotted content is missing and querySelector in the child returns null. Walk the checks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Match slot name, use this.querySelector for slotted nodes, confirm it is not Aura, and confirm the parent actually passed body markup.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I remember slotted nodes are not in the child's shadow tree, so this.template.querySelector misses them. Multiple unnamed slots duplicate content—usually have one. Dynamic slot attributes on fillers are coerced to strings. I do not debug CSS first.
interview_questions.example: Parent N and child ; child uses this.querySelector('span').
tradeoffs: Slots vs passing a badge string as @api
follow_ups: Can slot name be dynamic on the <slot> element?

interview_questions.question: When would you not split into parent/child?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When there is no reuse and no slot/property contract—just extra files. Also when a base component already is the child you need.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Composition pays off for reuse and for owner control of tickets and plates. A single small template can stay one bundle. lightning-button is composition with a base child. I will not split just to nest folders. Events across the page still are not this lesson.
interview_questions.example: Keep a 15-line banner in one LWC; extract labBadge only when two parents need the same badge plus slot.
follow_ups: What is an owner versus a Lightning page?
weak_answer_warnings: A child component for every paragraph

interview_questions.question: Teach parent/child with the pass-window analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Parent chef writes @api tickets, calls @api fire methods, and fills slot plates. constructor unlocks the station before tickets arrive. It breaks on owner versus container rank and on Aura not being garnish.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw the mermaid: parent HTML to child, properties down, methods called, slots filled, constructor then connectedCallback. I say folders are hallway siblings. I refuse generic catalog metaphors. I leave bubbling and LMS for the next topic.
interview_questions.example: labParent / labChild with name property, footer slot, ping method, constructor super only.
follow_ups: What must you not invent about other hooks?
